subject: design-technology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: A patent gives an inventor:
options: Permanent ownership of an idea forever
The right to copy others' products
A time-limited legal right to stop others making or selling their invention
Ownership of a brand name only
questions.explain: A patent grants a time-limited monopoly to exploit an invention in exchange for public disclosure.

questions.q: A primary aim of designing to reduce material use ('Reduce' in the 6 Rs) is to:
options: Use fewer resources and less energy, lowering environmental impact
questions.explain: Reducing material and energy use lowers resource depletion, cost and environmental impact.

questions.q: Glass-reinforced plastic (GRP) is classified as a composite because it:
options: Is a thermoplastic that can be remelted
Combines glass fibres with a polymer matrix to gain enhanced properties
questions.explain: A composite combines two or more materials—here glass fibres and resin—to achieve superior strength-to-weight properties.

questions.q: Designing a product to be repairable rather than disposable primarily supports which of the 6 Rs?
questions.explain: Making products serviceable and fixable embodies the 'Repair' principle, extending useful life.

questions.q: Inclusive (universal) design aims to create products that are:
options: Usable only by the average person
As cheap as possible regardless of usability
Usable by the widest possible range of people regardless of age or ability
questions.explain: Inclusive design seeks to make products accessible to as many users as possible, including those with disabilities.

questions.q: Which property describes a material's ability to be drawn into a wire?
questions.explain: Ductility is the ability to undergo tensile deformation, such as being drawn into wire, without fracturing.

questions.q: Quantum Tunnelling Composite (QTC) is a smart material whose electrical resistance:
options: Decreases sharply when compressed or deformed
questions.explain: QTC changes from an insulator to a conductor as pressure brings conductive particles closer together.

questions.q: Electroluminescent material is best described as a smart material that:
options: Emits light when an electric current is applied
questions.explain: Electroluminescent materials glow when a voltage is applied across them, used in flexible displays and safety wear.

questions.q: Modernism in design emphasised:
options: Mass-produced functional objects stripped of unnecessary ornament
questions.explain: Modernism embraced new materials and machine production with rational, functional, ornament-free forms.

questions.q: A Gore-Tex-style technical textile is described as breathable yet waterproof because its membrane:
options: Has pores too small for water droplets but large enough for water vapour
questions.explain: The microporous membrane lets vapour escape while keeping liquid water out, giving breathable waterproofing.

questions.q: Design for Disassembly (DfD) primarily supports sustainability by:
options: Making products impossible to take apart
Enabling components to be easily separated for repair, reuse or recycling
Reducing the number of recyclable materials used
questions.explain: DfD allows easy separation of parts and materials at end-of-life for recovery and recycling.

questions.q: Consumer protection legislation (e.g. the Consumer Rights Act) requires goods to be:
options: Of satisfactory quality, fit for purpose and as described
questions.explain: Consumer law requires that goods are of satisfactory quality, fit for purpose and match their description.

questions.q: Just-in-Time (JIT) manufacturing aims to:
options: Slow down the production line deliberately
Minimise inventory by receiving materials only as they are needed
Keep large stocks of raw materials
questions.explain: JIT reduces holding costs and waste by delivering materials precisely when required for production.

questions.q: The Memphis design group of the 1980s is characterised by:
options: Bold colours, playful geometric shapes and decorative patterns
questions.explain: Memphis rejected functionalism with vivid colours, bold patterns and playful, decorative forms.

questions.q: Art Deco design, popular in the 1920s-30s, is characterised by:
options: Sleek geometric forms, symmetry and luxurious decorative detail
questions.explain: Art Deco combined streamlined geometric forms with rich materials and decorative elegance.

questions.q: Vacuum forming is a process in which a heated thermoplastic sheet is:
options: Forced into a mould under high injection pressure
Drawn over a mould by removing the air beneath it
questions.explain: Vacuum forming sucks air from beneath a softened sheet so atmospheric pressure pulls it onto the mould.

questions.q: Planned obsolescence is a strategy in which products are:
options: Deliberately designed with a limited useful life to encourage replacement
Designed to last as long as technically possible
Sold without any warranty by law
questions.explain: Planned obsolescence intentionally limits product lifespan to drive repeat purchases.

questions.q: An alloy is best defined as:
options: A mixture of a metal with one or more other elements to improve properties
questions.explain: Alloys combine a base metal with other elements—e.g. steel is iron and carbon—to enhance properties.

questions.q: Anodising aluminium is carried out mainly to:
options: Build a protective, decorative oxide layer that resists corrosion
questions.explain: Anodising thickens the natural oxide layer, improving corrosion resistance and allowing colouring.

questions.q: Dieter Rams, associated with Braun, is best known for the design philosophy:
questions.explain: Dieter Rams championed minimalist functional design summarised as 'less, but better'.

questions.q: The iterative design process is best described as:
options: A single linear sequence completed once
A repeating cycle of designing, modelling, testing and refining
questions.explain: Iterative design repeatedly loops through prototyping and testing to progressively improve a solution.

questions.q: CIM (Computer Integrated Manufacturing) refers to:
options: The use of computers to control and integrate the entire manufacturing process
questions.explain: CIM links CAD, CAM and business systems so computers coordinate the whole production operation.

questions.q: Which testing method assesses a material's resistance to a sudden impact load?
questions.explain: Charpy and Izod tests strike a notched specimen to measure energy absorbed, indicating toughness.

questions.q: New and emerging technologies such as automation can impact employment by:
options: Eliminating the need for any human input ever
Reducing some routine manual roles while creating demand for new technical skills
Having no effect on the workforce
questions.explain: Automation displaces routine tasks but generates new roles requiring different, often higher, technical skills.

questions.q: Continuous production is characterised by:
options: Making products in limited identical groups
Running 24/7 to produce identical products without interruption
questions.explain: Continuous production runs non-stop, typical of chemicals or float glass, to make a constant flow of product.

questions.q: The circular economy model is based on the principle of:
options: Producing as much waste as possible
Keeping materials in use through reuse, repair and recycling to design out waste
questions.explain: The circular economy keeps resources in use as long as possible, eliminating the linear waste model.

questions.q: Which of these is one of the '6 Rs' of sustainable design?
questions.explain: The 6 Rs are Rethink, Refuse, Reduce, Reuse, Repair and Recycle.

questions.q: Forging improves the strength of a metal component primarily by:
options: Compressing and deforming the metal to refine and align its grain structure
Melting and pouring it into a mould
questions.explain: Forging plastically deforms metal, refining the grain flow to produce a stronger part than casting.

questions.q: CAM (Computer Aided Manufacture) most directly involves:
options: Using computer-controlled machines such as CNC routers to make parts
questions.explain: CAM uses software to drive CNC machinery that fabricates a designed part.

questions.q: Intellectual property in the form of a registered design protects:
options: The visual appearance, shape or pattern of a product
The functional invention inside a product
questions.explain: Registered design rights protect the look—shape, configuration and decoration—of a product.
